messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — I ran into a migration edge-case while testing per-tenant private endpoints. If we keep peering attachments long after a tenant is deprovisioned, stale routes leak and we get routing churn in the edge fabric.
Priya Kumar: Oof. Is this the route-advertisement TTL issue or leftover ENI/CIDR bindings?
Alex Chen: Leftover CIDR bindings. We tear down the endpoint resource but the peering object sticks around because of our async cleanup job failing during retries.
Ben Ortiz: That's the job we throttled last quarter to avoid API quotas, right?
Maya Singh: Yup. We backoff aggressively which means peering attachments can linger for hours. When they finally die, routes get flapped and customers report transient 5xx.
Jordan Lee: Two quick questions: (1) can we avoid route rewrites entirely by using NAT on the customer side? (2) can we mark peering as ephemeral so the control plane auto-forgets faster?
Priya Kumar: Re: NAT — we discussed NAT-on-customer for IP preservation earlier. It's workable but shifts complexity to the tenant and breaks some enterprise compliance who require source IP visibility.
Ben Ortiz: Ephemeral peering sounds promising. We can add a TTL label on peering objects and have the controller refresh while the endpoint is active. If the refresh fails X times, the peering is removed immediately.
Maya Singh: I like TTL label approach. Helps with orphan cleanup and reduces manual ops. But we need safe rollout so we don't accidentally drop still-in-use peerings due to transient control-plane hiccups.
Alex Chen: Agreed. Proposal: add ttl_seconds label + a refresh loop with exponential backoff but bounded retries (e.g., 6 attempts over 10 minutes). After that, mark peering for fast teardown and send an alert + reconciliation job kicks in.
Jordan Lee: Add a caveat: when teardown happens, we should advertise a temporary blackhole route to the edge-proxy so active connections drain instead of hard fail. That avoids instant 5xx.
Ben Ortiz: Implementation sketch:
```
metadata.labels: {
  "peering.ttl_seconds": "600"
}
controller: refresh every 60s (token bucket), retry 6 times, then annotate: peering/reap=true
reaper: sweep annotated peerings every 30s -> delete & advertise blackhole for 30s
```
Priya Kumar: Two followups: monitoring and cost. Frequent re-creates will increase peering API calls and possible cross-account attach charges. We should add token-level metrics (api_calls_peering_refresh) and a cost budget alert.
Maya Singh: Also need to consider cross-region customers — blackhole trick only works within same routing plane. For cross-region we should failover to regional relay rather than immediate delete.
Alex Chen: Good point — make peering TTL semantics region-aware. For cross-region endpoints, mark as "staged-reap" and escalate to human if refresh fails beyond threshold.
Jordan Lee: Ops playbook idea: when a peering goes into "staged-reap", notify tenant-ops + create a short-lived canary route that sends traffic to a probe endpoint. If probe fails for N minutes, then full reap.
Ben Ortiz: I can build a spike that implements TTL label, refresh loop, and reaper with blackhole advertising plus metrics. Suggest we run it behind a feature flag and enable for a handful of low-risk tenants.
Priya Kumar: +1. Also add a dashboard: peering_count_by_state, peering_refresh_attempts, peering_reap_rate, api_calls_peering_refresh. Alerts on reap_rate > 1/min per region.
Maya Singh: Can we queue the reaper deletes to small batches to avoid route-flap storms? Batch size 5 per region with jitter.
Alex Chen: Yes. Batching + jitter. Also add an opt-out annotation for customers that need long-lived static peering for compliance: `peering.persistence=sticky`.
infra-bot: Note: created issue INFRA-7382 for "peering TTL + reaper spike" and assigned to @Ben_Ortiz.
Jordan Lee: Next actions: Ben spike -> demo -> feature flag rollout for 10 tenants -> measure metrics for 48h -> expand. I'll create a rollout checklist.
Ben Ortiz: I'll start the spike today, will post PR and a minimal test plan.
Priya Kumar: Thanks — let's capture the decision in the RFC followup doc once spike validates. :thumbsup:
Maya Singh: And add a short-hand runbook for oncall — commands to list staged-peers and force-reap safely.
Alex Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
